items.stem:
Read the following excerpt from President Richard Nixon's address to the nation announcing the Vietnamization policy, November 3, 1969 (Richard Nixon, 'Address to the Nation on the War in Vietnam,' November 3, 1969; Public Papers of the Presidents of the United States, National Archives and Records Administration):

"I have initiated a plan which will end this war and serve the cause of peace — not just in Vietnam but in the Pacific and in the world. In the previous administration, we Americanized the war in Vietnam. In this administration, we are Vietnamizing the search for peace... The more support I can have from the American people, the sooner that pledge can be redeemed; for the more divided we are at home, the less likely the enemy is to negotiate at Paris. Let us be united for peace. Let us also be united against defeat. Because let us understand: North Vietnam cannot defeat or humiliate the United States. Only Americans can do that."

Using this excerpt and your knowledge of U.S. policy in Vietnam and the constitutional crisis that followed (US.80, US.82), write a constructed response that:
1. States a CLAIM about how Nixon's Vietnamization strategy and the constitutional conflicts it generated — including the War Powers Resolution and Watergate — together transformed the balance of power between the executive and legislative branches.
2. Provides EVIDENCE from the document and from your knowledge of key events from 1969 to 1974.
3. Explains your REASONING for how Vietnamization and Watergate together represent a turning point in executive power.

Your response should be 1–2 paragraphs —
items.stemEs:
Lee el siguiente fragmento del discurso del Presidente Richard Nixon a la nación anunciando la política de Vietnamización, 3 de noviembre de 1969 (Richard Nixon, 'Discurso a la Nación sobre la Guerra en Vietnam,' 3 de noviembre de 1969; Documentos Públicos de los Presidentes de los Estados Unidos, Administración Nacional de Archivos y Registros):

«He iniciado un plan que pondrá fin a esta guerra y servirá a la causa de la paz, no solo en Vietnam sino en el Pacífico y en el mundo. En la administración anterior, americanizamos la guerra en Vietnam. En esta administración, estamos vietnamizando la búsqueda de la paz... Cuanto más apoyo pueda tener del pueblo estadounidense, más pronto podrá cumplirse esa promesa; porque cuanto más divididos estemos en casa, menos probable será que el enemigo negocie en París. Seamos unidos por la paz. Seamos también unidos contra la derrota. Porque entendamos: Vietnam del Norte no puede derrotar ni humillar a los Estados Unidos. Solo los estadounidenses pueden hacer eso.»

Usando este fragmento y tu conocimiento de la política de EE. UU. en Vietnam y la crisis constitucional que siguió (US.80, US.82), escribe una respuesta construida que:
1. Formule un ARGUMENTO sobre cómo la estrategia de Vietnamización de Nixon y los conflictos constitucionales que generó —incluyendo la Resolución de Poderes de Guerra y Watergate— juntos transformaron el equilibrio de poder entre los poderes ejecutivo y legislativo.
2. Proporcione EVIDENCIA del documento y de tu conocimiento de eventos clave de 1969 a 1974.
3. Explique tu RAZONAMIENTO sobre cómo la Vietnamización y Watergate juntos representan un punto de inflexión en el poder ejecutivo.

Tu respuesta debe tener 1–2 párrafos.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score (4/4) response would include: CLAIM — Nixon's Vietnamization strategy, while framed as responsible de-escalation, deepened executive unilateralism (the secret bombing of Cambodia, the invasion of Cambodia in 1970) and, together with the Watergate scandal, provoked a decisive legislative reassertion of constitutional checks that permanently restructured the executive-legislative balance. EVIDENCE — The excerpt reveals Nixon's rhetorical strategy of framing domestic dissent as an obstacle to peace ('only Americans can do that'), which justified expanding the war covertly; the secret bombing of Cambodia (Operation Menu, 1969–1970) was conducted without congressional knowledge; the invasion of Cambodia in April 1970 triggered the Cooper-Church Amendment (1970) and Kent State; the War Powers Resolution (1973) passed over Nixon's veto, requiring the president to notify Congress within 48 hours of committing troops and obtain authorization within 60 days; the Watergate break-in (June 1972), the Saturday Night Massacre (October 1973), and Nixon's resignation (August 1974) compounded the constitutional crisis; the Articles of Impeachment included obstruction of justice and abuse of presidential power. REASONING — Both Vietnamization and Watergate reflected the same underlying belief in expanded executive prerogative, and Congress responded to both simultaneously: the War Powers Resolution curbed military unilateralism while the impeachment process and post-Watergate reforms (Congressional Budget and Impoundment Control Act of 1974 (Pub. L. 93-344), Freedom of Information Act amendments) rebuilt legislative oversight, marking the end of the 'imperial presidency.'
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.80, US.82 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (4 points):
4 - Exemplary: States a defensible claim that explicitly connects Vietnamization's executive overreach (US.80) to Watergate's constitutional crisis (US.82) as two faces of the same pattern of unchecked presidential power. Cites specific evidence from the document (rhetorical framing, 'only Americans can do that') and from knowledge (Cambodia bombing, Cooper-Church, War Powers Resolution, Watergate timeline, Nixon resignation). Reasoning explains the mechanism — that both crises together forced a structural legislative correction — and synthesizes across both standards.
3 - Proficient: States a clear claim connecting Vietnamization and Watergate to executive-legislative tension. Cites specific evidence from the document and from knowledge. Reasoning connects evidence to claim but may not fully synthesize across both standards or may treat them as parallel rather than interconnected.
2 - Developing: Addresses Vietnamization OR Watergate but not both in depth. Claim is present but underdeveloped. Evidence is general (mentions 'Cambodia' or 'Watergate' without specifics). Reasoning is descriptive rather than analytical.
1 - Beginning: Summarizes Nixon's speech without analysis. May list facts about Vietnam or Watergate without connecting them to the claim or to each other.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Nixon's rhetorical framing in the excerpt; Vietnamization as gradual troop withdrawal while training ARVN; secret bombing of Cambodia (Operation Menu, 1969); Cambodia invasion (1970) and Kent State reaction; Cooper-Church Amendment (1970); War Powers Resolution (1973) passed over Nixon's veto; Watergate break-in (June 1972); Saturday Night Massacre (October 1973); Nixon resignation (August 9, 1974); Articles of Impeachment citing obstruction and abuse of power.
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (4 puntos):
4 - Ejemplar: Formula un argumento defensible que conecta explícitamente el exceso ejecutivo de la Vietnamización (US.80) con la crisis constitucional de Watergate (US.82) como dos caras del mismo patrón de poder presidencial sin control. Cita evidencia específica del documento (encuadre retórico, 'solo los estadounidenses pueden hacer eso') y del conocimiento propio (bombardeo de Camboya, Cooper-Church, Resolución de Poderes de Guerra, cronología de Watergate, renuncia de Nixon). El razonamiento explica el mecanismo —que ambas crisis juntas forzaron una corrección legislativa estructural— y sintetiza ambos estándares.
3 - Competente: Formula un argumento claro que conecta la Vietnamización y Watergate con la tensión ejecutivo-legislativa. Cita evidencia específica del documento y del conocimiento propio. El razonamiento conecta la evidencia con el argumento pero puede no sintetizar completamente ambos estándares o puede tratarlos como paralelos en lugar de interconectados.
2 - En desarrollo: Aborda la Vietnamización O Watergate, pero no ambos en profundidad. El argumento está presente pero poco desarrollado. La evidencia es general. El razonamiento es descriptivo en lugar de analítico.
1 - Inicial: Resume el discurso de Nixon sin análisis. Puede enumerar hechos sobre Vietnam o Watergate sin conectarlos con el argumento o entre sí.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Encuadre retórico de Nixon en el fragmento; Vietnamización como retiro gradual de tropas mientras se entrenaba al Ejército de Vietnam del Sur; bombardeo secreto de Camboya (Operación Menú, 1969); invasión de Camboya (1970) y reacción de Kent State; Enmienda Cooper-Church (1970); Resolución de Poderes de Guerra (1973) aprobada sobre el veto de Nixon; allanamiento de Watergate (junio 1972); Masacre del Sábado por la Noche (octubre 1973); renuncia de Nixon (9 de agosto de 1974); Artículos de Acusación por obstrucción y abuso de poder.

items.stem:
DIRECTIONS: Analyze the three primary source excerpts below. Then write a response that constructs a historical argument answering the following question:

How did the convergence of the anti-war movement, the Kent State killings, and the Watergate crisis between 1969 and 1974 together erode public trust in the federal government, and what evidence suggests these events marked a fundamental shift in American political culture rather than a temporary crisis?

Your response must:
- Analyze at least TWO of the three documents using the SOAPS framework (Speaker, Occasion, Audience, Purpose, Significance)
- Synthesize evidence across documents to support a historical argument
- Connect to your own knowledge of events and long-term consequences beyond the documents
- Address standards US.79 and US.82

---
DOCUMENT 1
Source: 'Report of the President's Commission on Campus Unrest' (Scranton Commission), Chapter 3: 'The Events at Kent State,' September 26, 1970. U.S. Government Printing Office. Washington, D.C. (Public domain U.S. government document.)
Excerpt: "The May 4 shootings at Kent State University are an event that divided Americans deeply. The Commission believes it necessary to speak plainly: the indiscriminate firing of rifles into a crowd of students and the deaths that followed were unnecessary, unwarranted, and inexcusable. The guardsmen on Blanket Hill, fearful and anxious, may have believed they were in danger, but they were not. The deaths of four students and the wounding of nine others must be condemned."

---
DOCUMENT 2
Source: Vietnam Veterans Against the War (VVAW), 'Statement of John Kerry,' testimony before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, April 22, 1971. U.S. Senate Congressional Record, 92nd Congress, 1st Session. National Archives.
Excerpt: "We are here in Washington to say that the problem of this war is not just a question of war and diplomacy. It is part and parcel of everything that we are trying as human beings to communicate to people in this country — the question of racism, the question of a limited nuclear capability, the question of the use of this country as a tool to maintain a façade of democracy while actually it is run by a little group of men who make most of the decisions... We are also here to ask, and we are here to ask vehemently, where are the leaders of our country? Where is the leadership?"

---
DOCUMENT 3
Source: President Richard Nixon, 'Address to the Nation Announcing His Resignation,' August 8, 1974. Public Papers of the Presidents of the United States. National Archives and Records Administration.
Excerpt: "I have never been a quitter. To leave office before my term is completed is abhorrent to every instinct in my body. But as President, I must put the interests of America first... I have always tried to do what was best for the Nation. Throughout the long and difficult period of Watergate, I have felt it was my duty to persevere, to make every possible effort to complete the term of office to which you elected me. In the past few days, however, it has become evident to me that I no longer have a strong enough political base in the Congress to continue that effort... Therefore, I shall resign the Presidency effective at noon tomorrow."

---
Use SOAPS to analyze the documents, then construct your argument in 2–3 paragraphs.
items.stemEs:
INSTRUCCIONES: Analiza los tres fragmentos de fuentes primarias a continuación. Luego escribe una respuesta que construya un argumento histórico respondiendo la siguiente pregunta:

¿Cómo la convergencia del movimiento antibelicista, las matanzas de Kent State y la crisis de Watergate entre 1969 y 1974 erosionaron juntas la confianza pública en el gobierno federal, y qué evidencia sugiere que estos eventos marcaron un cambio fundamental en la cultura política estadounidense en lugar de una crisis temporal?

Tu respuesta debe:
- Analizar al menos DOS de los tres documentos usando el marco SOAPS (Orador, Ocasión, Audiencia, Propósito, Significado)
- Sintetizar evidencia de los documentos para apoyar un argumento histórico
- Conectar con tu propio conocimiento de eventos y consecuencias a largo plazo más allá de los documentos
- Abordar los estándares US.79 y US.82

---
DOCUMENTO 1
Fuente: 'Informe de la Comisión Presidencial sobre el Desorden en los Campus' (Comisión Scranton), Capítulo 3: 'Los Eventos en Kent State,' 26 de septiembre de 1970. Imprenta del Gobierno de EE. UU. Washington, D.C. (Documento gubernamental de dominio público de EE. UU.)
Fragmento: «Los disparos del 4 de mayo en la Universidad de Kent State son un evento que dividió profundamente a los estadounidenses. La Comisión considera necesario hablar con franqueza: los disparos indiscriminados de rifles contra una multitud de estudiantes y las muertes que siguieron fueron innecesarios, injustificados e inexcusables. Los guardias en Blanket Hill, temerosos y ansiosos, pueden haber creído que estaban en peligro, pero no lo estaban. Las muertes de cuatro estudiantes y las heridas de otros nueve deben ser condenadas.»

---
DOCUMENTO 2
Fuente: Veteranos de Vietnam contra la Guerra (VVAW), 'Declaración de John Kerry,' testimonio ante el Comité de Relaciones Exteriores del Senado, 22 de abril de 1971. Registro del Congreso de EE. UU., 92.º Congreso, 1.ª Sesión. Archivos Nacionales.
Fragmento: «Estamos aquí en Washington para decir que el problema de esta guerra no es solo una cuestión de guerra y diplomacia. Es parte integral de todo lo que nosotros, como seres humanos, intentamos comunicar a las personas en este país — la cuestión del racismo, la cuestión de una capacidad nuclear limitada, la cuestión del uso de este país como herramienta para mantener una fachada de democracia mientras en realidad es dirigido por un pequeño grupo de hombres que toman la mayoría de las decisiones... También estamos aquí para preguntar, y estamos aquí para preguntar con vehemencia, ¿dónde están los líderes de nuestro país? ¿Dónde está el liderazgo?»

---
DOCUMENTO 3
Fuente: Presidente Richard Nixon, 'Discurso a la Nación Anunciando su Renuncia,' 8 de agosto de 1974. Documentos Públicos de los Presidentes de los Estados Unidos. Administración Nacional de Archivos y Registros.
Fragmento: «Nunca he sido un rendidor. Dejar el cargo antes de que mi mandato esté completo es repugnante para cada instinto de mi cuerpo. Pero como Presidente, debo poner los intereses de Estados Unidos primero... Por lo tanto, renunciaré a la Presidencia con efecto a partir del mediodía de mañana.»

---
Usa SOAPS para analizar los documentos, luego construye tu argumento en 2–3 párrafos.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score (6/6) response would include: ARGUMENT — The Scranton Commission report, John Kerry's Senate testimony, and Nixon's resignation address together document not a single crisis but a cumulative institutional breakdown: the government killed its own students (Doc 1), veterans publicly accused the military of war crimes and the government of structural corruption (Doc 2), and the presidency itself collapsed under the weight of criminal conduct (Doc 3). Taken together, these three events between 1970 and 1974 produced a permanent restructuring of American political culture — a fundamental post-Vietnam, post-Watergate cynicism about government authority that polling data and post-1974 legislative responses confirm. SOAPS ANALYSIS (Doc 1) — Speaker: Presidential commission (Scranton Commission, appointed by Nixon); Occasion: aftermath of Ohio National Guard killing of four Kent State students, May 4, 1970; Audience: American public, Nixon, Congress; Purpose: investigate and officially assess the Kent State killings; Significance: a Nixon-appointed commission condemned the killings as 'unnecessary, unwarranted, and inexcusable,' representing the government's own admission of institutional failure and intensifying the credibility gap. SOAPS ANALYSIS (Doc 2) — Speaker: John Kerry, decorated Vietnam veteran and VVAW spokesman, later Senator; Occasion: VVAW's 'Dewey Canyon III' protest in Washington, D.C., April 1971; Audience: Senate Foreign Relations Committee and the American public; Purpose: expose war crimes and challenge the moral legitimacy of both the war and the government's conduct; Significance: veterans — the war's own participants — publicly withdrawing consent from the government's war narrative made the anti-war movement impossible to dismiss as cowardice or ignorance. SOAPS ANALYSIS (Doc 3) — Speaker: President Nixon, facing certain impeachment; Occasion: August 8, 1974, hours before the first presidential resignation in U.S. history; Audience: American people; Purpose: explain resignation while avoiding admission of criminal wrongdoing; Significance: the careful language ('political base in Congress') obscures the actual reason (criminal obstruction revealed by tapes), and that gap between rhetoric and reality is itself the culmination of the 'credibility gap' that began with the Gulf of Tonkin. SYNTHESIS — All three documents show leaders responding to crises they helped create, and all three reveal the gap between official language and documented reality. Outside knowledge: Gallup polling after Watergate showed government trust dropping to historic lows; Freedom of Information Act amendments (1974), the Church Committee investigations (1975), and campaign finance reform (FECA 1974) were direct legislative responses; Nixon's resignation was the first in U.S. history, setting a precedent that the constitutional system could hold even the president accountable.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.79, US.82 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.
items.explanation:
SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Constructs a defensible historical argument that directly addresses the prompt across US.79 and US.82. Analyzes all three documents using SOAPS accurately — speaker, occasion, audience, purpose, and significance are correctly identified for each and used analytically (not just listed). Synthesizes across documents to show cumulative erosion of trust. Integrates substantial outside knowledge (Gallup polling data, Church Committee, FECA 1974, Freedom of Information Act, or specific examples of institutional reform). Writing is clear, organized, and sustained across 2–3 paragraphs.
5 - Advanced: Constructs a defensible argument. Analyzes all three documents using SOAPS with minor gaps. Synthesizes across at least two documents. Includes relevant outside knowledge. Writing is organized.
4 - Proficient: Constructs a clear argument. Analyzes two of three documents using SOAPS. Some synthesis present. Includes some outside knowledge. Writing is adequate.
3 - Adequate: States a claim. Analyzes one or two documents with partial SOAPS. Limited synthesis. Minimal outside knowledge. Writing is underdeveloped.
2 - Developing: Describes document content without full SOAPS analysis. Claim is vague or implicit. Little synthesis. No meaningful outside knowledge.
1 - Beginning: Restates documents without analysis. No argument. No SOAPS. No synthesis.
0 - No response or completely off-topic.

DOCUMENT ANALYSIS EXPECTATIONS: Doc 1 — Scranton Commission as Nixon-appointed body condemning Kent State killings; significance of government self-condemnation; Doc 2 — Kerry as veteran/insider witness, VVAW's Dewey Canyon III occasion, Senate audience, purpose to delegitimize the war, significance of veterans as anti-war voice; Doc 3 — Nixon as resigning president, occasion of first-ever presidential resignation, audience as American people, purpose to frame resignation as sacrifice, significance of gap between stated reason (political base) and actual reason (criminal conduct).
KEY EVIDENCE EXPECTED: Kent State killings (May 4, 1970) and context of Cambodia invasion announcement; VVAW Winter Soldier Investigation (1971) and Dewey Canyon III; Watergate break-in (June 1972) through resignation (August 1974); Pentagon Papers and New York Times v. United States (1971); Gallup polling on government trust post-Watergate; Church Committee investigations (1975); Campaign Finance Reform (FECA 1974); War Powers Resolution (1973).
items.explanationEs:
GUÍA DE PUNTUACIÓN (6 puntos):
6 - Ejemplar: Construye un argumento histórico defensible que aborda directamente la pregunta en US.79 y US.82. Analiza los tres documentos usando SOAPS con precisión — el orador, la ocasión, la audiencia, el propósito y el significado se identifican correctamente para cada uno y se usan de manera analítica (no solo enumerados). Sintetiza entre documentos para mostrar la erosión acumulativa de la confianza. Integra conocimiento externo sustancial (datos de encuestas Gallup, Comité Church, FECA 1974, Ley de Libertad de Información, o ejemplos específicos de reforma institucional). La escritura es clara, organizada y sostenida en 2–3 párrafos.
5 - Avanzado: Construye un argumento defensible. Analiza los tres documentos usando SOAPS con pequeñas brechas. Sintetiza entre al menos dos documentos. Incluye conocimiento externo relevante. La escritura está organizada.
4 - Competente: Construye un argumento claro. Analiza dos de tres documentos usando SOAPS. Hay alguna síntesis. Incluye algún conocimiento externo. La escritura es adecuada.
3 - Adecuado: Formula un argumento. Analiza uno o dos documentos con SOAPS parcial. Síntesis limitada. Conocimiento externo mínimo. La escritura está poco desarrollada.
2 - En desarrollo: Describe el contenido del documento sin análisis SOAPS completo. El argumento es vago o implícito. Poca síntesis. Sin conocimiento externo significativo.
1 - Inicial: Reitera los documentos sin análisis. Sin argumento. Sin SOAPS. Sin síntesis.
0 - Sin respuesta o completamente fuera del tema.

EXPECTATIVAS DE ANÁLISIS DOCUMENTAL: Doc 1 — Comisión Scranton como organismo designado por Nixon que condena las matanzas de Kent State; significado de la autocondena gubernamental; Doc 2 — Kerry como testigo veterano/interno, ocasión de Dewey Canyon III del VVAW, audiencia del Senado, propósito de deslegitimar la guerra, importancia de los veteranos como voz antibelicista; Doc 3 — Nixon como presidente que renuncia, ocasión de la primera renuncia presidencial en la historia de EE. UU., audiencia del pueblo estadounidense, propósito de enmarcar la renuncia como sacrificio, importancia de la brecha entre la razón declarada (base política) y la razón real (conducta criminal).
EVIDENCIA CLAVE ESPERADA: Matanzas de Kent State (4 de mayo de 1970) y contexto del anuncio de la invasión de Camboya; Investigación del Soldado de Invierno del VVAW (1971) y Dewey Canyon III; Allanamiento de Watergate (junio 1972) hasta la renuncia (agosto 1974); Papeles del Pentágono y New York Times v. Estados Unidos (1971); Encuestas Gallup sobre la confianza gubernamental post-Watergate; Investigaciones del Comité Church (1975); Reforma de Financiamiento de Campañas (FECA 1974); Resolución de Poderes de Guerra (1973).
